He played [[college basketball]] for [[Virginia Commonwealth University]]. As a senior, he averaged 22.4 points, 6.2 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game in the [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09 season]]. Maynor was drafted by the [[Utah Jazz]] of the NBA in 2009. He has also played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Washington Wizards]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. ==Early years== Eric Demarqua Maynor was born June 11, 1987, in [[Raeford, North Carolina]], the third of four children of George Maynor and Barbara Robinson.[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/eric_maynor/bio.html "Eric Maynor,"] NBA.com, Retrieved Feb. 22, 2013. Maynor's father was a former collegiate basketball player at [[East Carolina University]] and was a fourth-round selection of the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[1979 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Maynor began at [[Hoke County High School]] in Raeford, then transferred to [[Westover High School (Fayetteville, North Carolina)|Westover High School]] in neighboring [[Fayetteville, North Carolina|Fayetteville]] for his senior year to play alongside his friend and AAU teammate De'shaune Griffin.This assertion as to the reason for the change of schools is unsourced but appears to be accurate, as De'shaune Griffin's father was an assistant boys' basketball coach at Westover High. See: [http://www.icgaels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=14900&ATCLID=822676 "#3 De'shaune Griffin,"] Iona College Gaels, www.icgaels.com Maynor led the team to the North Carolina state championship game, scoring 25 points in a loss to [[North Mecklenburg High School]] on March 14, 2005.Bob Gibbons, [http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?cid=398511 "State Champions Crowned in North Carolina,"] Rivals.com, www.collegebasketball.rivals.com/ March 14, 2005. For his outstanding performance during the season Maynor was named to the 2004/05 North Carolina All State Basketball team by the sports website NCPreps.com.Don Hines, [http://ncpreps.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=411320 "The NCPreps.com 2004-05 North Carolina All State Basketball Team,"] NCPreps.com/ April 27, 2005. ==College career== Eric Maynor was a four-year player in the men's basketball program at [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] (VCU). He graduated from VCU with a degree in Sports Management. ===Freshman season (2005–06)=== Maynor played in 29 games as a freshman at VCU, cracking the team's starting lineup by the end of the season. Maynor averaged 4.7 points and 2.2 assists in an average of 15.7 minutes per game during this first collegiate campaign. ===Sophomore season (2006–07)=== On March 15, 2007, Maynor scored 22 points, including the game-winning shot, in VCU's victory over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in the first round of the [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. Maynor's last-minute heroics are also what helped VCU to overcome [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] in the 2007 [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) championship game. Over the summer of 2007, Maynor was selected to represent the United States in the [[Pan American Games]], alongside [[D. J. White]] and [[Michael Beasley]]. Maynor was only able to play two games for the American Pan-Am team, however, before he was forced from further action by a hip injury. Maynor was also named one of the 50 pre-season candidates for the men's 2007–08 [[John R. Wooden Award]], the nation's most prestigious college basketball honor. ===Junior season (2007–08)=== Maynor helped VCU win the CAA regular-season title, though the team fell in the semi-finals of the conference tournament to [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]]. He was selected as the [[Colonial Athletic Association Men's Basketball Player of the Year|CAA Player of the Year]] and selected to the All-CAA first team.[http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=43048&SPID=3455&DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=1406497 VCU’S Maynor Headlines 2007-08: All-CAA Men's Basketball Team,"] CAA Hoop Scoop, www.caasports.com/ March 6, 2008. The Rams failed to reach the NCAA Tournament and went on to play in the NIT, where they lost in the first round against the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]]. ===Senior season (2008–09)=== During the 2008–09 season, Eric Maynor became VCU's all-time leader in assists[http://vcuathletics.tv/mbb/0809results/mbb-gameday.php "Regular Season Crown, Scoring Title on the Line Saturday at 4 pm,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110901042215/http://vcuathletics.tv/mbb/0809results/mbb-gameday.php |date=2011-09-01 }} VCU Rams Basketball, www.vcuathletics.tv/ Feb. 28, 2009. and in made free throws. On February 28, 2009, Maynor became the leading scorer in VCU history with a floater against [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State]]. As of March 10, 2009, he had scored a school record 1,929 points. Maynor also led VCU to a second CAA title during his career, scoring 25 points in a 71–50 victory over George Mason on March 9, 2009, at the [[Richmond Coliseum]]. The Rams went on to the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009 NCAA Tournament]] but lost to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] when Maynor missed a buzzer-beater to win the game. ==Professional career== ===NBA=== ====Utah Jazz (2009)==== Maynor was drafted 20th overall by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/maynoer01.html|title = Eric Demarqua Maynor | publisher= Basketball-Reference.Com|access-date= December 10, 2012}} He became the first VCU player ever selected in the first round of the NBA draft. Maynor signed a two-year contract with the Jazz on July 1, 2009, and made $1.3 million in his rookie season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/07/01/Jazz.Maynor.ap/index.html?rss=true |title=Rookie Maynor signs two-year deal with Jazz |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2009-07-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108191333/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/07/01/Jazz.Maynor.ap/index.html?rss=true |archive-date=2012-11-08 |url-status=dead }} Although he was to back up [[Deron Williams]], Maynor had a positive outlook on the situation. When asked in an interview with RealCollegeBasketball.com what he thought about coming off the bench in Utah, Maynor replied, "Feel real good about it... I'm getting a chance to learn from some of the best".{{Cite web |url=http://realcollegebasketball.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=256:eric-maynor-interview&catid=51:interview |title=RealCollegeBasketball.com's Interview With Eric Maynor |access-date=2009-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110825181541/http://realcollegebasketball.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=256:eric-maynor-interview&catid=51:interview |archive-date=2011-08-25 |url-status=dead }} ====Oklahoma City Thunder (2009–2013)==== On December 22, 2009, Maynor, along with [[Matt Harpring]], was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the rights to [[Peter Fehse]].[http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder_aquires_maynor_2009_12_22.html "Thunder Acquires Maynor From Utah Jazz,"] NBA.com, Dec. 22, 2009. According to a statement made by Jazz general manager [[Kevin O'Connor (basketball)|Kevin O'Connor]] at the time of the deal, the trade of Maynor along with the $6.5 million contract of the injured power forward Harpring was made for financial reasons, in an effort to reduce the team's liability under the NBA's punitive "luxury tax" on teams with excessive salaries.Associated Press, [https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4766058 "Maynor Headed to Thunder,"] via ESPN.com Dec. 23, 2009. "Trading Eric was a difficult decision," O'Connor acknowledged, while noting that the team remained strong at the point guard position with star Deron Williams and [[Ronnie Price]] as a capable and proven reserve player. Maynor wound up as the backup point guard on the young Thunder team behind the emerging superstar [[Russell Westbrook]], drafted by the franchise as the #4 overall pick one year prior to Maynor coming into the NBA. On January 7, 2012, the Thunder reported that Maynor had torn his right [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) in the fourth quarter of Oklahoma City's 98–95 win over the [[Houston Rockets]] and would miss the remainder of the season. Without Maynor the Thunder reached the [[2012 NBA Finals]], but lost in five games to the [[Miami Heat]]. ====Portland Trail Blazers (2013)==== In a deal concluded just 30 minutes before the noon trade deadline on February 21, 2013, Maynor was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the NBA rights to [[Georgios Printezis]].Mike Tokito, [http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2013/02/blazers_acquire_point_guard_eric_maynor_without_sa.html#incart_river "Late Trade Lands Backup Point Guard: Eric Maynor Moves from Thunder Bench to Playing time with Blazers,"] ''The Oregonian,'' Feb. 22, 2013; pp. D1, 5. Maynor was averaging just 2.8 points and 2.0 assists in an average of about 10.6 minutes per game playing for the Thunder and had fallen to number three on the team's depth chart for point guards, with second-year player [[Reggie Jackson (basketball, born 1990)|Reggie Jackson]] emerging to capture most of the team's backup PG minutes.Ben Golliver, [http://www.blazersedge.com/2013/2/21/4014308/reports-blazers-agree-to-trade-for-thunder-g-eric-maynor "Blazers Trade For Thunder G Eric Maynor; Waive Ronnie Price,"] ''Blazers Edge,'' Feb. 21, 2013. The Blazers were forced to waive reserve point guard Ronnie Price to make room on the team's 15-man roster for Maynor. Portland general manager [[Neil Olshey]] was effusive about Maynor's style of play and his fit for the club, calling Maynor "a great guy to run our second unit while being able to play with our starters." Olshey noted that Maynor was known for making excellent decisions with the basketball while playing at a steady and reliable pace and offered the possibility that Maynor might potentially share time in the backcourt with Blazer rookie star [[Damian Lillard]]. Olshey expressed hope that Maynor would mesh well with the team and make a solid long-term addition to the roster, declaring:
"You don't make moves just for 28 games, but clearly there's going to be an evaluation curve for us where we're going to have to evaluate Eric, see how he fits in with our team, our style of play, our culture.... We'll see what kind of opportunities present themselves."
==== Washington Wizards (2013–2014) ==== On July 10, 2013, Maynor signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-eric-maynor|title=Wizards Sign Eric Tournament=== In 2017, Maynor participated in [[The Basketball Tournament]] for Ram Nation, a team of VCU alumni. Maynor averaged 13.5 PPG, 7.3 APG, and 5.5 RPG to help Ram Nation reach the Elite 8. In the Elite 8, Ram Nation lost a close game to the eventual tournament champs, [[Overseas Elite]].
